title: Payment Operations Standard — Where the Re-dating Clock Starts on Payment Arrangements
content:
For a plan under Payment Arrangements, the re-dating clock start follows how and when the plan's most recent returned installment payment arrived.

## Standard

The return lag is the number of calendar days from the scheduled due date of the returned installment to the date the return was received, both read from the most recent returned installment payment on the plan's installment history.

1. When the most recent return was for account closed or stop payment and was received no more than the type's automatic-debit grace period in calendar days after the scheduled due date, the re-dating clock starts on the date the return was received.
2. When it was for unauthorized debit or card chargeback and was received no more than that many days after the scheduled due date, the re-dating clock starts on the scheduled due date.
3. Any other return starts the re-dating clock on the handling date — this covers a return for NSF, and a return of any reason received more days after the scheduled due date than that grace period.

## The grace period that sets the threshold

| Arrangement type | Automatic-debit grace period (calendar days) |
|---|---|
| Promise-to-Pay Arrangement | 0 |
| Short-Term Installment Plan | 3 |
| Standard Installment Plan | 5 |
| Extended Installment Plan | 7 |
| Long-Term Installment Plan | 7 |
| Hardship Reduced-Payment Plan | 10 |

## Input — judgement — output

| Return reason | Return lag compared with the grace period | Clock starts on |
|---|---|---|
| Account closed or stop payment | Not more than the grace period | The date the return was received |
| Account closed or stop payment | More than the grace period | The handling date |
| Unauthorized debit or card chargeback | Not more than the grace period | The scheduled due date of the returned installment |
| Unauthorized debit or card chargeback | More than the grace period | The handling date |
| NSF | Any | The handling date |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, Standard Installment Plan, grace 5 days)

- A stop-payment return on an installment due 1 June, received 6 June: lag 5 days, not more than 5 — the clock starts on 6 June.
- The same return received 7 June: lag 6 days, more than 5 — the clock starts on the handling date.
- A card chargeback on an installment due 1 June, received 4 June: lag 3 days — the clock starts on 1 June.
- On a Promise-to-Pay Arrangement the grace is 0 days, so only a return received on the scheduled due date itself meets the first two rows.
